questions.q: What business problem does the Northfield Outdoor Supply scenario start from?
options: On-premises SQL Server data with only a nightly manual spreadsheet export, and a need for same-day visibility without hiring a dedicated DBA
A company that already has a fully built cloud data platform and wants a redesign
A company with no data at all, starting completely from scratch
A purely theoretical exercise with no stated business goal
questions.explain: Northfield's real constraint is manual, delayed reporting off an on-prem database, and the goal is same-day visibility without a full-time DBA hire.

questions.q: In the end-to-end pipeline this capstone builds, what is Glue's role between S3 and Redshift?
options: Cataloging the raw data (crawler) and transforming it with an ETL job before it loads into Redshift
Storing the final, queryable data permanently instead of Redshift
Replacing the need for S3 entirely
Sending email alerts when the pipeline fails
questions.explain: Glue sits in the middle: a crawler catalogs the raw S3 data, then a Glue ETL (Spark) job transforms it before it's loaded into Redshift.

questions.q: What service orchestrates the whole Northfield pipeline on a schedule, per this lesson?
options: Step Functions
CloudWatch
IAM
Athena
questions.explain: Step Functions is named as the orchestrator that sequences and schedules the pipeline so nobody has to kick it off manually.

questions.q: What does Chapter 3 of this capstone add on top of the working pipeline from Chapter 2?
options: Production practices: CloudWatch monitoring, IAM least privilege, CI/CD, cost optimization, and disaster recovery
An entirely new, unrelated business scenario
A rebuild of the pipeline using only the AWS console, no code
Nothing — Chapter 3 just repeats Chapter 2's lessons
questions.explain: Chapter 3, 'Adding Production Practices,' is explicitly about monitoring, security, CI/CD, cost, and DR — turning a working demo into a job-ready project.

questions.q: Why does this capstone stick with one concrete scenario (Northfield) instead of building each AWS service's feature in isolation with generic sample data?
options: So every AWS service choice has a stated business reason tied to Northfield's real constraints, not just 'because the course said so'
Because AWS requires all tutorials to use a single named company
Because using more than one scenario is technically impossible in AWS
There is no stated reason — it's an arbitrary choice
questions.explain: The guide explicitly ties service decisions (like S3 storage classes or Redshift cluster vs. serverless) to Northfield's real, stated business constraints.
